classes.name: Loop diuretics
classes.description: Loop diuretics: furosemide (Lasix; tablets, oral solution; Furoscix subcutaneous on-body infusor and Lasix ONYU subcutaneous, alternatives only, never the pick), torsemide (generic; Soaanz), bumetanide (Bumex), ethacrynic acid (Edecrin; for sulfa allergy). Not thiazides.
classes.plainDescription: A strong water pill that removes extra fluid, for heart failure, kidney and liver disease and swelling.

preferredAgent.sig: Edema: 20 to 80 mg by mouth as a single dose; repeat or raise by 20 or 40 mg no sooner than 6 to 8 hours later until the response is right (label). Check potassium.
preferredAgent.plainSig: One pill in the morning. Your dose may be adjusted to how much fluid you lose.

records.verificationNote: Not a PDL class: the PDL legend says any therapeutic class not listed "will continue to be covered" for DC Medicaid fee-for-service members (p. 6). Coverage and restrictions for this class are not in the document; absence from the PDL is not treated as exclusion. The PDL has no standalone loop diuretic class. The only diuretic entries are combinations with ACE inhibitors, ARBs and beta blockers (pp. 17-19). Furosemide, torsemide, bumetanide, ethacrynic acid (Edecrin), Lasix, Lasix ONYU, Furoscix and Soaanz are not printed anywhere in the PDL. Absence is not exclusion. The 20 mg starting dose is label dosing; the PDL prints none. [Sonnet check 2026-11-24: absence from the PDL re-confirmed by page-text grep of all 70 pages; no change.]
